pages.title: Dinosaur Coloring Book Prompts for Kids & KDP
pages.metaDescription: Dinosaur coloring page prompts for five 24-page books, page by page: baby dinos, dino jobs, a fossil dig, prehistoric eras and adult patterns.
pages.intro: Dinosaurs are one of the steadiest sellers in kids' coloring on Amazon KDP and Etsy, because every generation of children goes through a dinosaur phase. Here are five dinosaur coloring books of 24 pages each, written out page by page: baby dinosaurs at home for toddlers, dinosaurs with jobs and sports, a fossil dig and museum trip, a realistic prehistoric world by era, and intricate patterned dinosaurs for adults. Copy one page at a time into ChatGPT, Gemini or any AI image tool, or copy all 24 and make the whole book.
tips: Keep the toddler book about one big dinosaur doing one familiar thing per page; parents of 2-5 year olds buy recognisable routines, not roaring predators.
Mix famous species (T-rex, triceratops, stegosaurus) with lesser-known ones like therizinosaurus and pachycephalosaurus so the Look Inside preview shows real variety.
The fossil-dig and museum angle pairs well with museum gift shops and school trips, so list it with paleontology keywords as well as dinosaur ones.

pages.title: Farm Animal Coloring Book Prompts: Cute Barnyard Pages
pages.metaDescription: Farm animal coloring page prompts for five 24-page books, page by page: baby animals, named animals, farm seasons, a county fair and farmhouse art.
pages.intro: Farm animals are often the very first animals a toddler learns to name, which makes a farm animal coloring book a perfect first coloring book and a dependable KDP seller. Here are five farm coloring books of 24 pages each, written out page by page: baby barnyard animals for toddlers, 24 farm animals and breeds with their names, a year of seasons on the farm, a day at the county fair, and patterned farmhouse animals for adults. Copy one page at a time into ChatGPT, Gemini or any AI image tool, or copy all 24 and make the whole book.
keywords: farm animal coloring pages for toddlers
tips: Baby animals (chicks, piglets, lambs, calves) outsell adult farm animals for the under-5 crowd; lead the cover and first pages with them.
A named-animal book with one animal per page doubles as a first-words book, so you can list it under early learning as well as coloring.
Seasonal farm scenes like spring lambing, pumpkin harvest and a snowy barn let one farm book rank for several gift seasons.

prompts.name: Four seasons on the farm

fields.description: 24 farm scenes through one year, six for each season. Spring: a newborn lamb in the barn, planting with a tractor, a muddy calf in the rain, sheep shearing. Summer: baling hay, milking a cow, picking strawberries, gathering honey, a farm stand. Autumn: a pumpkin patch, apple picking, a corn maze with a scarecrow, a hayride, the harvest. Winter: a snowy barn, feeding horses in the snow, collecting eggs on a frosty morning, a horse-drawn sleigh.

pages.intro: Sea creatures work for every age, from a toddler's first smiling whale to an adult colorist's intricate jellyfish mandala, and teachers use them for ocean units. These ocean animal coloring book prompts cover five 24-page books: sea friends for toddlers, tide pools and beach life, sharks and ocean giants, the deep sea, and an under the sea mandala collection. pages.title: Unicorn Coloring Book Prompts: Unicorns & Magical Creatures
pages.metaDescription: Unicorn coloring book prompts for five 24-page books, page by page: baby unicorns, unicorn parties, magical creatures, a forest quest and mandalas.
pages.intro: Unicorn coloring books are a perennial best seller on Amazon KDP, especially as birthday and holiday gifts for kids aged 4 to 10. Here are five unicorn coloring books of 24 pages each, written out page by page: baby unicorns on clouds for toddlers, unicorns at parties and hobbies, a kingdom of magical creatures, an enchanted forest quest for tweens, and ornate unicorn mandalas for teens and adults. Copy one page at a time into ChatGPT, Gemini or any AI image tool, or copy all 24 and make the whole book.
tips: Plain unicorn books are crowded on KDP; a magical creatures book with pegasus, griffins and fairies widens the keywords you can rank for.
Give every page an activity (a tea party, a carousel, a sleepover) so the unicorns are doing something, not just standing in a field.

pages.title: Dragon Coloring Book Prompts for Kids, Teens & Adults
pages.metaDescription: Dragon coloring book prompts for five 24-page books, page by page: silly baby dragons, elemental dragons, dragon riders, Eastern dragons and adult art.
pages.intro: Dragons sit at the crossroads of fantasy and adventure, so a dragon coloring book appeals to boys and girls alike and keeps selling to teens and adults too. Here are five dragon coloring books of 24 pages each: silly baby dragons for little kids, a different dragon for every element, a dragon riders' academy for tweens, flowing Eastern dragons and festivals, and an intricate collection for adult colorists. Each book is written out page by page, so you can paste one page at a time into ChatGPT, Gemini or any AI image tool, or copy all 24 and make the whole book.
tips: For under-6s, make dragons silly instead of fierce: tiny puffs of fire, wobbly first flights and toasted marshmallows keep the book gift-friendly.
An elemental book (fire, ice, forest, storm, crystal) means a 24-page book never repeats the same dragon in a new pose.
Eastern dragons sell year-round and spike before Lunar New Year, so list that book in January with festival keywords.

pages.title: Jungle & Safari Animal Coloring Book Prompts
pages.metaDescription: Jungle safari coloring prompts for five 24-page books, page by page: baby animals, a jungle explorer trip, rainforest layers, the savanna and mandalas.
pages.intro: Jungle and safari animals are a classic coloring theme that never fades: lions, elephants, giraffes and monkeys are instantly recognisable, and kids love the adventure of a safari. Here are five jungle and safari coloring books of 24 pages each: baby animals with their mothers for toddlers, a jungle explorer adventure, rainforest animals layer by layer, savanna wildlife and the great migration, and safari mandalas for adults. Each book is written out page by page, so you can paste one page at a time into ChatGPT, Gemini or any AI image tool, or copy all 24 and make the whole book.
keywords: jungle animal coloring book for kids
zoo animal coloring book for toddlers
tips: Keep rainforest and savanna in separate books; each then ranks for its own keywords and the pages barely overlap.
For toddlers, show baby animals with their mothers; for older kids, add explorers, jeeps and rope bridges to make it an adventure.
Elephants, lions and giraffes carry mandala patterns beautifully, which makes safari a good crossover into the adult market.

pages.intro: Cat lovers are one of the most loyal buyer groups on Amazon KDP and Etsy, and cat coloring books sell to kids, teens and adults alike. pages.title: Dog & Puppy Coloring Book Prompts for Kids and Adults
pages.metaDescription: Dog and puppy coloring book prompts for five 24-page books, page by page: playful puppies, hero dogs, 24 breeds, a dog's day out and adult portraits.
pages.intro: Dogs are a top-selling coloring theme because almost every family has, or wants, a dog. Here are five dog and puppy coloring books of 24 pages each, written out page by page: playful puppies for toddlers, working and helper dogs, 24 dog breeds with names, a day of dog parks, groomers and dog shows, and patterned dog portraits for adults. Copy one page at a time into ChatGPT, Gemini or any AI image tool, or copy all 24 and make the whole book.
tips: A dog breeds book lets owners find their own dog, which is a strong selling point in the listing and the Look Inside preview.
Puppy books for toddlers sell best with action: fetching, digging, splashing and bath time.
A working-dogs book (rescue, guide, police, farm dogs) doubles as a community-helpers book for teachers.

pages.title: Bird Coloring Book Prompts: Cute Birds, Bird Names & Mandalas
pages.metaDescription: Bird coloring book prompts for five 24-page books, page by page: baby birds, backyard birds, birds of the world, owls and raptors, and floral mandalas.
pages.intro: Bird coloring books suit toddlers who love owls, penguins and ducklings, nature-loving families who want the real birds at their feeders, tweens who like eagles and falcons, and adult colorists who adore peacocks and hummingbirds among flowers. Here are five bird coloring books of 24 pages each: baby birds for toddlers, backyard birds and feeders, 24 birds of the world with names, owls and birds of prey, and floral bird mandalas for adults. Every book is written out page by page, so you can paste one page at a time into ChatGPT, Gemini or any AI image tool, or copy all 24 and make the whole book.
keywords: bird mandala coloring pages for adults
tips: A backyard-birds book works best with the birds your buyers actually see, like robins, cardinals and chickadees at feeders and birdbaths.
Owls and birds of prey are the most-searched birds for coloring, so they can carry a whole book of their own.
For adults, pair birds with flowers (hummingbirds with hibiscus, herons with lotus) to cross into the botanical coloring market.

pages.intro: Vehicle coloring books are a top seller for kids who love anything with wheels, wings or a horn. Here are five vehicle coloring books of 24 pages each, written out page by page: a construction site for toddlers, rescue and emergency vehicles, 24 named planes, boats and trains, fast machines for big kids, and classic cars and vintage travel for teens and adults. Every vehicle is unbranded, so the books are safe to sell, and you can paste one page at a time into ChatGPT, Gemini or any AI image tool, or copy all 24 and make the whole book.

pages.title: Princess & Castle Coloring Book Prompts (Original Characters)
pages.metaDescription: Princess and castle coloring book prompts for five 24-page books, written page by page: tea parties, brave princesses, many lands, gowns and castles.
pages.intro: Princess coloring books are a perennial gift for young children, and fairy-tale castles keep their charm right into the adult coloring market. Here are five princess and castle coloring books of 24 pages each with original characters: a sweet little-princess day for toddlers, a knights-and-dragons adventure, princesses from many lands, a royal gown fashion book for teens, and ornate fairy-tale castles for adults. Each is written out page by page, so you can paste one page at a time into ChatGPT, Gemini or any AI image tool, or copy all 24 and make the whole book.
tips: Use only original princesses: anything that looks or sounds like a film character can get a KDP listing removed.
Brave, active princesses (archery, inventing, dragon riding) set your book apart from dress-only books.
A gown fashion book and a castle architecture book reach teens and adults who have outgrown tea-party pages.

pages.title: Mermaid Coloring Book Prompts for Kids, Teens & Adults
pages.metaDescription: Mermaid coloring page prompts for five 24-page books, page by page: baby mermaids, an undersea kingdom, seven seas, cozy days and ornate portraits.
pages.intro: Mermaid coloring books combine magic and the ocean, and they sell as gifts from preschool to the tween years and to a strong adult audience. Here are five mermaid coloring books of 24 pages each with original characters: baby mermaids and sea friends for toddlers, a whole undersea kingdom, merfolk from Arctic ice to mangrove swamps, cozy everyday mermaid life for teens and adults, and ornate mermaid portraits. Each one is written out page by page, so you can paste one page at a time into ChatGPT, Gemini or any AI image tool, or copy all 24 and make the whole book.
keywords: under the sea mermaid coloring pages
tips: Keep every mermaid original; avoid famous red-haired film mermaids and their sidekicks so the book is safe to sell.
Put a sea friend (turtle, otter, octopus) on most pages; it keeps a mermaid book varied.
Include merboys and mermaids of different looks, which broadens the gift audience.

pages.title: Robot Coloring Book Prompts for Kids & Tweens
pages.metaDescription: Robot coloring book prompts for five 24-page books, written page by page: toddler robots, town jobs, robot animals, giant mechs and steampunk machines.
pages.intro: Robot coloring books appeal to kids who love building and gadgets, and they make a good STEM-flavoured gift. Here are five robot coloring books of 24 pages each: friendly boxy robots for toddlers, a town where robots do every job, animals rebuilt as robots, giant mechs for teens, and brass steampunk automatons for adult colorists. Each book is written out page by page, so you can paste one page at a time into ChatGPT, Gemini or any AI image tool.
tips: Pitch robot books as STEM gifts in your listing; parents searching for science gifts are a wider audience than robot fans alone.
Toddler robots work best boxy, big-eyed and busy with everyday jobs like baking or gardening.
Avoid shape-shifting car robots and other famous designs; robot animals, mechs and steampunk bots are safe, original angles.

pages.intro: Animal mandala coloring books combine the calm of pattern coloring with the pull of a favourite animal. These prompts cover five 24-page books: easy pet and garden animals for kids, ocean creatures and mythical beasts for tweens, and bird and wild animal mandalas for teens and adults. Each book is written out page by page, one patterned animal per page, so you can paste one page at a time into ChatGPT, Gemini or any AI image tool.

animal mandala coloring book for kids
tips: List a different animal for every page; animal mandala buyers expect variety, not ten owls.
Ask for each animal against a matching floral or wave backdrop for a full-page design.
Pick animals with strong silhouettes (elephant, owl, turtle, fox); they read clearly even when filled with pattern.

pages.title: Stress Relief Coloring Book Prompts for Adults
pages.metaDescription: Stress relief coloring book prompts for five 24-page books, written page by page: calm shores, bedtime scenes, mandalas, a large-print garden and tweens.
pages.intro: These stress relief coloring book prompts are for adults who want a quiet way to slow down away from screens, for seniors who need bigger, simpler pictures, and for tweens getting through exam season. Each of the five books keeps to one setting: calm shores, a night-time wind-down, intricate pattern meditations, a large-print garden and everyday calm breaks for tweens. Every book is written out page by page, 24 pages each, so you can paste one page at a time into ChatGPT, Gemini or any AI image tool.
keywords: stress relief coloring book for adults
tips: Lean on slow, quiet subjects (still water, sleeping animals, rain, candlelight); calm scenes beat busy ones for this buyer.
Keep pages without words; many anxiety-relief buyers find affirmations distracting and prefer to let the picture do the work.
Give each book in the series one clear setting (shore, night, garden) so buyers can pick the one that relaxes them.

pages.title: Bold and Easy Coloring Book Prompts for Adults & Seniors
pages.metaDescription: Bold and easy coloring prompts for five 24-page books, written page by page: retro nostalgia, cute animals, sweet treats, little houses and beach days.
pages.intro: Bold and easy coloring books have big, simple shapes and large areas to fill, which makes them a top seller for adults who want quick relaxation, seniors, people with low vision and anyone using markers. Here are five bold and easy books of 24 pages each, one clear subject per page: retro nostalgia for seniors, cute animal friends, sweet treats and snacks, little houses and shops, and a day at the beach. Each book is written out page by page, so you can paste one page at a time into ChatGPT, Gemini or any AI image tool.
keywords: bold and easy coloring book prompts
bold and easy coloring book for adults
large print coloring book for seniors
coloring book for people with dementia
tips: Keep to one main subject per page; a teacup or a cactus with a few props reads better than a crowded scene.
Choose familiar, friendly objects; recognisable subjects are what make bold and easy books relaxing.
Market the books for alcohol markers and gel pens; big areas suit them and that is how buyers search.

pages.title: Flower & Botanical Coloring Book Prompts
pages.metaDescription: Flower and botanical coloring book prompts for five 24-page books, written page by page: vintage botanicals, bouquets, houseplants and wildflowers.
pages.intro: Flower and botanical coloring books are bought year-round by gardeners, nature lovers and adult colorists, and they are a favorite gift around Mother's Day and in spring. These five books each run 24 pages: an intricate vintage botanical edition, bouquets and flower-shop arrangements, succulents and houseplants, wildflowers with their pollinators for tweens, and big friendly flowers for preschoolers. Every book is written out page by page, so you can paste one page at a time into ChatGPT, Gemini or any AI image tool.
tips: Name real flowers (peony, foxglove, magnolia, iris); specific species look far better than a generic 'flower'.
For the botanical edition, ask for leaves, buds, seed pods and roots too; it gives the vintage herbarium look buyers want.
Time flower books for spring and Mother's Day, when gift searches for floral coloring books peak.

prompts.why: Adult colorists and gardeners pay a premium for realistic botanical detail, and the vintage herbarium angle stands out from generic flower books.
prompts.pageStyle: Black-and-white adult coloring page in the style of a vintage herbarium plate: one realistic, botanically accurate plant study centered on the page with its stems, leaves, buds and seeds, fine crisp outlines, detailed petals and leaf veins with many small areas to color, little or no background, no shading, no grey, no hatching, no words or labels, plain white background, portrait 8.5 x 11 page.

pages.title: Christmas Coloring Book Prompts for Kids & Adults
pages.metaDescription: Christmas coloring book prompts for five 24-page books, written page by page: toddlers, Santa's workshop, snow days, a cozy village and mandalas.
pages.intro: Christmas is the biggest seasonal sale of the year on Amazon KDP and Etsy, and demand starts in October. Here are five Christmas coloring books of 24 pages each, running from toddlers to adults: a first Christmas book for ages 3-6, a Santa's workshop adventure for ages 6-9, snow-day fun for tweens, a cozy village for adults and an intricate book of ornament and snowflake mandalas. Each one is written out page by page, so you can paste one page at a time into ChatGPT, Gemini or any AI image tool.
tips: Publish Christmas books by early October; the search peak runs from November to mid-December.
Mix classic symbols (stockings, wreaths, gingerbread) with full scenes so a 24-page book is not 24 lone ornaments.
Give the kids' and adult books one series name so buyers who find one find the rest.

pages.title: Halloween Coloring Book Prompts for Kids & Adults
pages.metaDescription: Halloween coloring page prompts for five 24-page books, written page by page: spooky-cute toddlers, a monster party, a haunted manor and mandalas.
pages.intro: Halloween coloring books sell from September through October to parents, teachers and adults who love the season. Here are five Halloween coloring books of 24 pages each: spooky-cute pumpkins and ghosts for ages 3-6, a monster party for ages 6-9, a room-by-room haunted manor for tweens, a witchy spooky-cozy cottage for adults and intricate moonlit mandalas. Each one is written out page by page, so you can paste one page at a time into ChatGPT, Gemini or any AI image tool, and the kids' books stay friendly, with no gore and no scary faces.
keywords: spooky cozy coloring book for adults
tips: Keep ghosts and monsters smiling for kids; spooky-cute sells, scary returns.
For adults, 'spooky-cozy' (witch cottages, candles, black cats, apothecary shelves) outsells horror on KDP.
Publish by early September so the books are indexed before the October rush.

pages.title: Easter & Spring Coloring Book Prompts
pages.metaDescription: Easter and spring coloring book prompts for five 24-page books, written page by page: toddler bunnies, an egg hunt, spring outdoors and folk-art eggs.
pages.intro: Easter and spring coloring books are basket fillers: parents, grandparents and teachers buy them in March and April, and adults pick up patterned egg and nature books for the season. These five prompts each make a 24-page book: bunnies and chicks for toddlers, an egg-hunt adventure for ages 6-9, spring outdoors for tweens, realistic baby animals for adults and an intricate book of folk-art decorated eggs. Every book is written out page by page, so you can paste one page at a time into ChatGPT, Gemini or any AI image tool.
tips: Market Easter books as basket stuffers; it is the phrase gift buyers search.
Mix Easter and general spring scenes (rain, gardens, baby animals) so the books sell beyond Easter week.
For adults, folk-art egg patterns give a seasonal twist on the mandala niche.

pages.title: Alphabet ABC Coloring Book Prompts for Toddlers & Preschool
pages.metaDescription: Alphabet coloring page prompts for five ABC books of 24 to 26 pages, written page by page: animals, first words, phonics, jobs and a floral alphabet.
pages.intro: Alphabet coloring books sell all year to parents, preschool teachers and homeschoolers teaching letters. Here are five ABC coloring books written out page by page: an animal alphabet parade and a first-words picture dictionary for toddlers, a phonics book of letter sounds, vowels and letter teams, an A to Z of jobs and where people work, and a 24-page floral alphabet with numbers for adult colorists. The four A to Z books have 26 pages, one letter per page; copy one page at a time into ChatGPT, Gemini or any AI image tool, or copy them all and make the whole book.
tips: An alphabet is exactly 26 pages, so keep one letter per page and fold the extras into the same scenes (a vowel's long sound, a letter team, the workplace) instead of padding the book with repeats.
Pick words a child can say and picture; 'D drum' teaches the letter, 'D dulcimer' does not.
Sell the toddler books and the phonics book as a set; the parent buying one usually has a child heading into the next stage.

pages.title: Numbers & Counting Coloring Book Prompts for Kids
pages.metaDescription: Five 24-page counting coloring book prompts, written page by page: count to 8 three ways, numbers 1 to 20, make-ten math, ocean 1 to 40 and times tables.
pages.intro: Counting coloring books help children link a number to an amount, and parents, preschool teachers and homeschoolers use them at every stage. These five 24-page books cover counting to 8 three ways, numbers with a numeral page and a counting page, make-ten and teen-number math, counting to 40 under the sea, and times tables as equal groups. Each one is written out page by page with its caption, so you can paste one page at a time into ChatGPT, Gemini or any AI image tool.
tips: Write each page as a number and its objects ('7 crabs') so the count on the page matches the caption.
Use small, separate objects (pebbles, bubbles, pearls) for numbers above 20 so children can count them one by one.
For math pages, give one object per section (ladybugs for make-ten, cookies for doubles) so the page changes but the method stays the same.

pages.title: Shapes and Colors Coloring Book Prompts for Preschool
pages.metaDescription: Five 24-page shapes and colors coloring book prompts, written page by page: first shapes, first colors, 3D solids, 24 color names and tween geometry.
pages.intro: Shapes and colors are among the first things children learn, so these books suit parents, preschool teachers and homeschoolers from toddler to middle school. Here are five 24-page books: eight basic shapes in everyday things, eight first colors, 3D solids with shape hunt scenes, twenty-four color names, and a geometry book for tweens. Each one is written out page by page, so you can paste one page at a time into ChatGPT, Gemini or any AI image tool.
tips: Give each shape or color several real objects (three each fills 24 pages for eight shapes) so a child sees the same idea in new places.
In a colors book the caption is the instruction: the child colors the page in the named color, so pick objects that really are that color.
Shape hunt scenes work best in places children know (a kitchen, a playground), where there is plenty to spot.

pages.title: Good Habits & Manners Coloring Book Prompts for Kids
pages.metaDescription: Five good habits and manners coloring books of 24 pages each, written page by page: toddler routines, animal manners, manners by place, health and tweens.
pages.intro: Good habits coloring books turn routines and manners into something children want to do, which is why parents, preschool teachers, counsellors and homeschoolers keep buying them. Here are five 24-page books with one habit per page and its caption: a toddler's day from morning to night, kind manners shown by animal friends, manners at the table, at school, in town and as a guest, health and safety habits, and responsibility for tweens. Each one is written out page by page, so you can paste one page at a time into ChatGPT, Gemini or any AI image tool.
keywords: daily routine coloring pages for toddlers
tips: Phrase every habit as an action ('carrying my plate to the sink') so each page is one clear picture with a caption that says what to do.
Group the 24 habits by time of day or by place; the book then reads in order and works as a routine chart.
Keep each book to its own age: toddlers want getting dressed and bath time, tweens want chores, money and screen habits.

pages.title: Feelings & Emotions Coloring Book Prompts for Kids
pages.metaDescription: Five 24-page feelings coloring book prompts, written page by page: animal feelings, feeling words, a calm-down toolbox, tween moments and emotion weather.
pages.intro: Feelings coloring books give children words for what they feel, and parents, preschool teachers, school counsellors and homeschoolers use them for social-emotional learning. These five 24-page books cover eight feelings shown by baby animals, 24 feeling words, a calm-down toolbox of 24 strategies, 24 real-life moments for tweens, and 24 emotions pictured as weather and nature for teens and adults. Each one is written out page by page, so you can paste one page at a time into ChatGPT, Gemini or any AI image tool.
keywords: calm down coloring book for kids
tips: Pair a feeling with a moment ('sad: a balloon floating away'); a situation teaches more than a face.
Use animal characters for little ones, so a child can talk about a feeling without it being about them.
Counsellors often buy a feelings book and a calm-down book together; list them as a pair.

prompts.name: Eight feelings with animal friends

fields.description: A first feelings book: eight feelings, each shown by baby animals in three moments, one per page with the feeling as its caption. Happy: puppy with a new ball, piglet in mud, lamb on a swing. Sad: lost balloon, washed-away sandcastle, broken toy train. Angry: tower knocked over, skipped in line, tangled kite. Scared: thunder, a dark bedroom, owlet's first flight. Surprised: a present, first snow, a surprise party. Proud: tying a shoelace, winning a race, a drawing. Shy: new friends, first school day, hiding behind mom. Calm: hammock, cloud watching, slow breathing.
fields.title: How Do You Feel, Little Friends?

prompts.why: Preschool teachers and parents use animal feelings books to start conversations, and three moments per feeling help a child see that a feeling can come from many things.
prompts.pageStyle: Black-and-white coloring page for a child aged 3 to 6: one big, cute cartoon baby animal with a clear, easy-to-read face filling most of the page, thick bold outlines, large simple shapes with wide spaces to color, very little background, no shading, no grey, the feeling word in big outlined letters at the bottom as the only words on the page, plain white background, portrait 8.5 x 11 page.

prompts.name: Calm-down toolbox

fields.description: A calm-down book of 24 strategies, one per page with its caption, each showing a child using it when upset. Breathing: flower and candle breaths, balloon breaths, five-finger breathing. Moving: a stress ball, wall push-ups, stretching like a cat, shaking out the wiggles, a self-hug. Senses: five things I can see, calm music, cold water, a soft blanket, a stuffed animal. Quiet time: a cozy corner, a book, a glitter jar, drawing how I feel, a journal. pages.title: Greek Mythology Coloring Book Prompts
pages.metaDescription: Greek mythology coloring book prompts for five 24-page books, written page by page: nature myths, a creature bestiary, hero quests, gods and the Odyssey.
pages.intro: Greek mythology coloring books are for kids who devour myth stories, homeschoolers teaching ancient history, and teens and adults who love epic heroes and monsters, and because the myths are public domain they are a safe niche for KDP sellers. Here are five books of 24 pages each: nature myths that explain the seasons and the stars for ages 6 to 9, a bestiary of legendary creatures, the heroes' quests in order, a gallery of gods, Titans and Muses for adults, and the Trojan War and the Odyssey in story order. Each book is written out page by page, so you can paste one page at a time into ChatGPT, Gemini or any AI image tool.
keywords: greek mythology coloring book for adults
greek mythology coloring book for kids
tips: Name the exact myth moment (Perseus with the mirrored shield, Odysseus tied to the mast) rather than just the hero; scenes sell better than portraits.
Keep the monsters dramatic without gore: the Minotaur in the labyrinth works, the fight's aftermath does not.
Homeschoolers pair these with ancient history units, so a book that tells the Trojan War or Hercules' labors in order sells well to them.

prompts.name: Nature myths for kids: why things are the way they are

fields.description: 24 pages of Greek nature myths for kids, one scene per page, each myth explaining something in the world: Prometheus bringing fire, Pandora's jar with Hope inside, Athena's olive tree, Hermes' tortoise-shell lyre, Pan's reed pipes, Echo and Narcissus, Daphne the laurel tree, Arachne's weaving contest, King Midas' golden touch, Baucis and Philemon's jug, Arion and the dolphin, the halcyon birds, Icarus' wings, Phaethon's sun chariot, Persephone and the seasons, the Great Bear stars, Eos at dawn and Selene's moon.
fields.title: Why the Seasons Change and Other Greek Myths

prompts.why: Parents and teachers want a way into the classic myths for ages 6 to 9, and myths that explain seasons, spiders and stars answer questions kids already ask.
prompts.pageStyle: Black-and-white coloring page for a child aged 6 to 9: one clear moment from a Greek myth with friendly, expressive characters in simple ancient Greek tunics and sandals, clear bold outlines, medium detail with a simple background that shows where the story happens, nothing scary, no shading, no grey, no words or letters, plain white background, portrait 8.5 x 11 page.
pages: Prometheus, a tall smiling Titan, tiptoeing down a cloudy mountain path from Mount Olympus, a glowing ember of fire hidden inside a hollow fennel stalk in his hand.
Prometheus kneeling beside a small family outside their stone hut, showing them how to light a cooking fire, a clay pot over the flames and a dog watching.
Pandora, a curious girl in a long tunic, lifting the lid of a big painted clay jar, little winged bugs flying out and one tiny bright butterfly named Hope still inside.
The goddess Athena in her helmet tapping the rocky ground with her spear as an olive tree springs up full of olives, the people of Athens cheering beside a half-built temple.
Baby Hermes in a cradle in a cave, strumming the first lyre he made from a tortoise shell and strings, the empty shell's pattern clear and a cow peeking in.
Pan, a friendly goat-legged god, sitting on a riverbank blowing into a row of tied reed pipes, music notes drifting over the water and reeds swaying around him.
Echo, a mountain nymph, cupping her hands by her mouth and calling out from a rocky cliff, swirly lines bouncing back from the mountains across the valley.
Narcissus, a young man, kneeling at the edge of a still pool and gazing at his reflection, a white narcissus flower beginning to bloom on the bank beside him.
Daphne standing by a river in a forest, her arms turning into leafy branches and her toes growing roots as she becomes a laurel tree, birds landing on her new leaves.
Arachne and the goddess Athena sitting side by side at two tall wooden looms in a weaving contest, their woven pictures half finished and baskets of wool at their feet.
A small spider spinning a beautiful round web between two olive branches, Arachne's empty weaving stool and a spindle of thread underneath it.
King Midas in his crown at a banquet table, laughing in surprise as the grapes, the bread and the cup he touches all turn to shining gold.
King Midas kneeling in a sparkling river and washing his hands, the golden touch flowing away as shiny gold flakes into the sand of the riverbed.
Old Baucis and Philemon in their tiny cottage pouring milk for two travelers, the clay jug magically refilling itself and a goose hiding under the bench.
Arion the musician riding on the back of a leaping dolphin across the waves, holding his lyre high, a ship sailing away in the distance.
Alcyone and her husband as two kingfisher birds sitting on a floating nest on a calm sea, gentle waves around them and the sun shining in a clear sky.
Icarus and his father Daedalus standing on a tower by the sea, strapping on big wings made of feathers and wax, a few loose feathers drifting in the wind.
Phaethon gripping the reins of the golden sun chariot as four wild horses gallop through the sky, the blazing sun behind him and clouds tumbling below.
Persephone picking flowers in a spring meadow as Hades, king of the underworld, pulls up beside her in a chariot to take her to his kingdom, her flower basket tipping over.
Persephone climbing up out of a cave into the sunlight as Demeter runs to hug her, flowers bursting up and fruit trees blooming all around them.
A great mother bear and her cub rising up into the night sky, the stars of the Great Bear and Little Bear shining on their backs above a sleeping village.
Eos, goddess of the dawn, flinging open two tall golden gates at the edge of the world, rays of morning light and a rooster crowing on a fence below.
Helios driving his four-horse sun chariot high across the midday sky, a farmer and his ox resting under a tree in a field of wheat far below.
Selene, goddess of the moon, driving a silver chariot pulled by two white horses across the night sky, a big crescent moon behind her and stars all around.

prompts.name: Bestiary of legendary creatures

fields.description: A bestiary of 24 legendary creatures from Greek myth, one per page, each in its home: a centaur in a forest, a satyr with pan pipes, a dryad in an oak, a naiad in a river, a nereid on a dolphin, Triton with his conch, a hippocamp, Pegasus, a griffin, a phoenix, the Sphinx outside Thebes, the Chimera, Cerberus at the underworld gates, Medusa, the Minotaur, the Python of Delphi, Ladon round the golden apple tree, Cetus, Scylla, the Sirens, a harpy, a cyclops by his cave, Talos guarding Crete and Argus with a hundred eyes.
fields.title: Beasts of Greek Myth

prompts.why: Tweens who love monsters and fantasy books, and homeschoolers studying ancient Greece, both buy creature bestiaries, and twenty-four creatures covers far more than the famous few.
prompts.pageStyle: Black-and-white coloring page for ages 9 to 13: one legendary creature from Greek myth as the large main subject in its home, fine clean outlines, detailed scales, feathers, fur, rocks and plants with many separate areas to color, dramatic but never gory, no shading, no grey, no words, plain white background, portrait 8.5 x 11 page.
pages: A centaur with a bow across his back trotting through an ancient oak forest, his horse body muscular and his long hair tied back, ferns and a fallen log at his hooves.
A satyr with curled horns and goat legs sitting on a mossy rock in a vineyard, playing a set of pan pipes, grape clusters hanging from the vines above him.
A dryad stepping halfway out of the trunk of a huge oak tree, her hair turning into leaves and acorns, an owl perched on the branch above her.
A naiad sitting on a smooth stone in the middle of a rushing mountain river, pouring water from a clay jug, small fish leaping and reeds along the banks.
A nereid riding on the back of a leaping dolphin across the open sea, her hair streaming behind her, seashells in her hair and spray rising from the waves.
Triton, half man and half fish, rising out of the waves and blowing a huge spiral conch shell, his long scaly tail curling through the water behind him.
A hippocamp, a horse with a long coiling fish tail and finned legs, galloping through a kelp forest on the sea floor, coral and starfish below.
Pegasus, the winged horse, rearing on a rocky mountaintop with his great feathered wings spread wide, a spring of water bubbling from the rock under his hoof.
A griffin with an eagle's head and wings and a lion's body guarding a nest of golden eggs on a cliff ledge, its talons gripping the rock.
A phoenix with long flowing tail feathers rising from a nest of cinnamon sticks, curling flames around it and the sun rising behind a desert ridge.
The Sphinx, with a lion's body, eagle's wings and a woman's calm face, sitting on a high rock above the road to Thebes, the city walls in the distance.
The Chimera, a lion with a goat's head rising from its back and a snake for a tail, prowling across a rocky hillside with small flames puffing from its mouth.
Cerberus, the huge three-headed dog, standing guard at the dark stone gates of the underworld, each head with a spiked collar, the river Styx behind him.
Medusa with a crown of writhing snakes for hair, standing in a shadowy cave, her face calm and fierce, stone statues of birds and a goat around her.
The Minotaur, with a bull's head and a man's body, standing in a stone corridor of the twisting labyrinth, torches on the walls and passages branching off.
The Python of Delphi, a giant serpent, coiled around the rocks of a mountain spring below the temple, steam rising from a crack in the ground.
Ladon, a many-headed dragon, coiled around the trunk of a tree heavy with golden apples in the garden of the Hesperides, flowers and a fountain nearby.
Cetus, an enormous sea monster with a long snout, fins and a scaly back, surging out of the waves toward a rocky coast, seabirds scattering above it.
Scylla, a sea monster with six long dog-headed necks, reaching out from a cave in a tall sea cliff, waves crashing against the rocks below.
Three Sirens with women's faces and birds' wings and feet sitting on a jagged rock in the sea, one playing a lyre, a ship sailing past in the distance.
A harpy with a woman's face, long wild hair and the wings and claws of a bird, swooping down over a rocky shore, feathers drifting behind her.
A one-eyed cyclops sitting at the mouth of his cave on a mountainside, carving a club from a tree trunk, a flock of fat sheep grazing around him.
Talos, a giant bronze man with riveted armor plates, striding along the cliffs of Crete and lifting a boulder, ships with sails out at sea below.
Argus, a giant covered in a hundred open eyes, sitting under an olive tree and watching over a white cow, a peacock with eye-patterned feathers beside him.

prompts.name: Quests of the Greek heroes

fields.description: The great Greek hero quests in 24 scenes, one per page, in story order. Hercules: the Nemean lion, the hydra, the golden hind, the Augean stables, the Stymphalian birds, holding up the sky for Atlas, Cerberus. Perseus: winged sandals, the Graeae's eye, the mirrored shield and Medusa, rescuing Andromeda. Theseus: his father's sword, Ariadne's thread, the Minotaur. Jason: one sandal, building the Argo, the clashing rocks, the bronze bulls, the sleeping dragon. Then Atalanta's race, Orpheus' lyre and Eurydice, Psyche's ants and Bellerophon on Pegasus.
fields.title: Quests of the Greek Heroes

prompts.why: Middle-grade myth fans and homeschoolers want the hero stories told in order, and seven of Hercules' labors plus seven other heroes' quests make a book that teaches the stories as well as being colored.
prompts.pageStyle: Black-and-white coloring page for ages 9 to 13: an action scene from a Greek hero's quest in a classical ancient Greek style, fine clean outlines, detailed armor, creatures, ships and landscape with many separate areas to color, exciting but never gory, no shading, no grey, no words, plain white background, portrait 8.5 x 11 page.
pages: Hercules wrestling the Nemean lion at the mouth of its rocky cave, his club dropped on the ground and his arms locked around the lion's thick mane.
Hercules swinging a flaming torch at the many-headed hydra rising from a swamp, his friend Iolaus behind him holding another torch among the reeds.
Hercules creeping through a snowy forest toward the golden hind, a deer with shining golden antlers, a hunting net slung over his shoulder.
Hercules digging a channel so two rivers rush through the filthy Augean stables, water surging past the stalls and cattle watching from a hill.
Hercules shaking a pair of bronze rattles beside a marsh as a flock of metal-feathered Stymphalian birds bursts into the sky, his bow ready.
Hercules straining to hold up the whole starry sky on his shoulders while Atlas walks back with three golden apples from the garden of the Hesperides.
Hercules leading the three-headed dog Cerberus on a chain out of the underworld gates into daylight, each of the dog's heads snarling.
Perseus strapping on a pair of winged sandals while Hermes hands him a curved sword and Athena holds out a polished bronze shield.
Perseus snatching the single shared eye from the three grey-haired Graeae sisters as they pass it between them at the mouth of a misty cave.
Perseus walking backward through Medusa's cave, watching her snake-haired reflection in his mirrored shield, stone statues standing in the shadows.
Perseus flying on winged sandals toward Andromeda, chained to a sea rock, as the sea monster Cetus rises from the waves below them.
Young Theseus heaving a huge boulder aside to find his father's sword and sandals hidden underneath, his mother watching from beside an olive tree.
Princess Ariadne handing Theseus a ball of red thread at the dark entrance of the labyrinth on Crete, guards asleep against the wall.
Theseus facing the Minotaur in a torchlit corner of the labyrinth, his sword raised and the thread unwinding behind him along the stone floor.
Jason arriving at King Pelias' court wearing only one sandal, the other lost in the river behind him, the king rising from his throne in alarm.
Shipbuilders hammering the long wooden hull of the Argo on a beach, Jason checking the carved prow while Athena fits a talking oak branch into it.
The Argo rowing hard between two huge clashing cliffs, a dove flying ahead and the rocks closing just behind the ship's stern.
Jason yoking two fire-breathing bronze bulls to a plow in a field, smoke puffing from their nostrils and King Aeetes watching from a stone wall.

Orpheus playing his lyre on a hillside as a bear, a deer, a wolf and birds gather peacefully around him, and even the trees lean in to listen.
Orpheus leading Eurydice up a steep, dark tunnel out of the underworld, his lyre in one hand and a glimmer of daylight at the top of the path.
Psyche kneeling beside a huge mixed pile of grain as an army of ants helps her sort the seeds into neat heaps, a lamp glowing beside her.
Bellerophon riding the winged horse Pegasus through the sky, his spear aimed at the fire-breathing Chimera on the mountainside below.

prompts.name: Gods, Titans and Muses for adults

fields.description: 24 intricate portraits of Greek gods, Titans and Muses, one per page, each with their symbols and setting. The twelve Olympians: Zeus, Hera, Poseidon, Demeter, Athena, Apollo, Artemis, Ares, Aphrodite, Hephaestus, Hermes and Dionysus. Hades and Persephone in the underworld. The Titans Gaia, Kronos and Atlas, and the three Fates spinning thread. Six pages of Muses: Calliope, Clio, Euterpe, Terpsichore, Thalia and Melpomene with their masks, and Urania with her star globe.
fields.title: Gods of Olympus: A Mythology Coloring Book

prompts.why: Teen and adult fans of myth want an intricate gallery of the whole pantheon, Muses included, and public-domain gods make it a safe KDP niche.
prompts.pageStyle: Black-and-white adult coloring page: a detailed classical portrait of a Greek god, Titan or Muse with their symbols, fine crisp line work, intricate drapery, hair, armor and ornaments, Greek key and laurel border details, many small areas to color, a balanced composition that fills the page, no shading, no grey, no words, plain white background, portrait 8.5 x 11 page.
pages: Zeus seated on a marble throne on Mount Olympus, a thunderbolt raised in one hand, an eagle on the armrest and storm clouds swirling behind him.
Hera standing in a flowing robe and tall crown, a peacock spreading its eye-patterned tail behind her and a pomegranate in her hand, columns at her sides.
Poseidon rising from crashing waves with his trident, his beard flowing like water, two hippocamps rearing beside him and shells and coral at his feet.
Demeter in a field of ripe wheat holding a sheaf of grain and a torch, poppies and a cornucopia of fruit around her and a plowed hill behind.
Athena in a crested helmet holding a spear and round shield, an owl perched on her shoulder and an olive branch with fruit framing the scene.
Apollo playing a lyre with a laurel wreath in his hair, the sun's rays fanning out behind his head and a swan and a raven at his feet.
Artemis drawing her bow in a moonlit forest, a quiver of arrows on her back, a deer leaping beside her and a crescent moon above.
Ares in a crested bronze helmet and breastplate gripping a spear and shield, a vulture and a wolf beside him and a battle standard behind.
Aphrodite in a flowing draped gown rising from a scallop shell on the sea, doves circling her, roses and sea foam swirling around the shell.
Hephaestus at his forge striking a glowing blade on an anvil, sparks flying, hammers and tongs on the wall and a bronze mechanical owl on a shelf.
Hermes in his winged cap and winged sandals running through the clouds, holding his caduceus with two twined snakes, a tortoise-shell lyre at his hip.
Dionysus reclining on a couch wrapped in grapevines and ivy, a wine cup and a thyrsus staff in his hands, a leopard lounging at his feet.
Hades on a dark throne in the underworld, a two-pronged staff in his hand, Cerberus lying at his feet and the river Styx flowing behind.
Persephone in a crown of spring flowers holding a split pomegranate, half her robe patterned with blossoms and half with underworld asphodel.
Gaia, Mother Earth, rising from the land with mountains on her shoulders, her hair becoming forests and rivers, animals sheltering in her robe.
Kronos, the Titan of time, standing with a great curved sickle, an hourglass at his feet and the wheel of the seasons turning behind him.
Atlas kneeling on a mountaintop as he holds the starry sphere of the heavens on his shoulders, the constellations etched across the globe.
The three Fates in a vaulted hall: Clotho spinning thread from a spindle, Lachesis measuring it with a rod and Atropos holding her shears.
Calliope, Muse of epic poetry, seated with a writing tablet and stylus, a laurel crown in her hair and a scroll unrolled across her lap.
Clio, Muse of history, standing beside a stack of scrolls and holding one open, a trumpet at her side and a carved column behind her.
Euterpe, Muse of music, playing a double flute in a garden, songbirds around her and musical instruments carved into a marble bench.
Terpsichore, Muse of dance, twirling with a lyre, her robes swirling in wide arcs around her and flower petals scattered on the floor.
Thalia, Muse of comedy, holding a laughing mask, and Melpomene, Muse of tragedy, holding a weeping mask, standing together on an ancient stage.
Urania, Muse of astronomy, pointing a rod at a large globe of the stars, a night sky full of constellations and planets curving above her.

prompts.name: The Trojan War and the Odyssey in order

fields.description: The Trojan War and the voyage of Odysseus in 24 scenes, one per page, in story order. The Trojan War: the golden apple, the judgment of Paris, Helen sailing to Troy, the thousand ships, Achilles in his tent, Hephaestus forging his shield, Hector's farewell, Priam asking for his son, the wooden horse rolled into Troy, soldiers climbing out at night. The Odyssey: the lotus-eaters, escaping the cyclops, Aeolus' winds, Circe, the Sirens, Scylla and Charybdis, Calypso's island, Poseidon's storm, Nausicaa, Athena's disguise, Argos the dog, Penelope's loom, the bow contest and the olive-tree bed.
fields.title: From Troy to Ithaca

prompts.why: Adult colorists, classics fans and high-school teachers want the epics in order, so the book works as a retelling of Homer as well as a coloring book.
prompts.pageStyle: Black-and-white adult coloring page: a dramatic, detailed scene from the Trojan War or the voyage of Odysseus in a classical ancient Greek style, fine crisp outlines, detailed ships, armor, drapery, waves and architecture with many small areas to color, a full scene that fills the page, intense but never gory, no shading, no grey, no words, plain white background, portrait 8.5 x 11 page.
pages: At a wedding feast of the gods, Eris tossing a golden apple onto the banquet table as Hera, Athena and Aphrodite all reach for it among wine cups and garlands.
Young Paris, a shepherd on Mount Ida, holding out the golden apple to Aphrodite while Hera and Athena stand beside her and his sheep graze nearby.
Paris and Helen sailing away from Sparta on a ship with a painted eye on its prow, Helen looking back at the shore and gulls wheeling over the sails.
A thousand Greek warships with rows of oars and tall sails setting out across the sea, banners flying and a coastline of temples behind them.
Achilles sitting in his tent by the shore, refusing to fight, his lyre on his knees and his armor and helmet hanging from the tent pole.
Hephaestus at his anvil hammering the great round shield of Achilles, its surface covered in tiny scenes of cities, fields and the circling ocean.
Hector in his plumed helmet saying goodbye to his wife Andromache on the walls of Troy, their baby son reaching out to touch the helmet's crest.
Old King Priam kneeling before Achilles in his tent at night, asking for his son's body, a lamp glowing between them and gifts piled at the entrance.
Trojans hauling the enormous wooden horse through the city gates on rollers, garlands hung on it, crowds cheering and towers rising above them.
Greek soldiers climbing down a rope ladder from a hatch in the wooden horse's belly in the moonlit city square, torches and sleeping guards nearby.
Odysseus dragging a sleepy sailor back to the ship from an island of lotus-eaters, who lounge among strange flowers offering fruit.
Odysseus and his men clinging beneath the bellies of big woolly rams as the giant cyclops sits blindly at the mouth of his cave, feeling the sheep's backs.
Odysseus' sailors untying the leather bag of winds while he sleeps on deck, gusts bursting out and the island of Ithaca vanishing on the horizon.
The enchantress Circe at her loom in a marble palace, offering a cup to Odysseus while his crew, turned into pigs, snuffle around the floor.
Odysseus tied to the mast of his ship, straining against the ropes, while his crew row with wax in their ears past the Sirens on their rocky island.
Odysseus' ship steering through a narrow strait between the swirling whirlpool Charybdis and Scylla's long necks reaching from a cliff cave.
Odysseus building a raft on the beach of Calypso's island, cutting logs with a bronze axe while Calypso watches from her vine-covered cave.
Poseidon rising from a furious storm and smashing Odysseus' raft with a huge wave, Odysseus clinging to a single beam in the churning sea.
Princess Nausicaa and her maids playing ball by a river where laundry dries on rocks, as Odysseus peers out from behind an olive bush.
Athena touching Odysseus with her staff on the shore of Ithaca, turning him into a ragged old beggar with a staff and a patched cloak.
Old Argos, Odysseus' faithful dog, lifting his head and wagging his tail as his disguised master walks past the palace gate.
Penelope at her loom at night, secretly unpicking the day's weaving by lamplight while suitors feast noisily in the hall below.
Odysseus, still in rags, drawing his great bow and shooting an arrow through the rings of twelve axe heads lined up in the palace hall.
Odysseus and Penelope embracing beside their bed carved from a living olive tree, its branches spreading over the bedroom in the palace.

pages.title: Bible Story Coloring Book Prompts for Kids & Adults
pages.metaDescription: Bible story coloring book prompts written page by page: five 24-page books of Bible animals, Old Testament stories, Jesus' life, parables and scripture.
pages.intro: Bible story coloring books are a steady seller for Christian parents, Sunday school teachers, church groups and homeschoolers, with peaks at Easter and Christmas. Here are five Bible story coloring books of 24 pages each: animals of the Bible for toddlers, Old Testament stories in order, the life of Jesus from the angel's visit to Pentecost, twenty-four parables Jesus told, and detailed scripture-inspired scenes for adult colorists, all drawn from public-domain stories. Each book is written out page by page, so you can paste one page at a time into ChatGPT, Gemini or any AI image tool, or copy all 24 and make the whole book.
tips: Name the exact moment (Zacchaeus up the sycamore tree, the walls of Jericho falling) so each page is recognisable.
For children's books choose the moment before the danger: David with his sling facing Goliath, Daniel among the lions.
Sunday school teachers buy books that follow the Bible's order, so one Old Testament book and one life-of-Jesus book can run a whole year.

prompts.name: Animals of the Bible for little ones

fields.description: 24 animals from Bible stories, one big friendly animal per page, each in its story: creation fish and birds, giraffes and elephants boarding the ark, the lion and lamb asleep on the ark, the dove with an olive leaf, Rebekah's camels, the frogs of Egypt, Balaam's donkey, David's lamb, Daniel's calm lions, Jonah's big fish, the ox and donkey at the manger, the wise men's camels, five loaves and two fish, the lost sheep, the mother hen and the Palm Sunday donkey.
fields.title: Animals of the Bible

prompts.why: Christian parents and nursery Sunday school teachers want a first Bible book toddlers can color, and an animal on every page is the way into each story.
prompts.pageStyle: Black-and-white coloring page for a child aged 3 to 6: one big, cute, friendly cartoon animal filling most of the page, thick bold outlines, large simple shapes with wide spaces to color, very little background, nothing scary, no shading, no grey, no words, plain white background, portrait 8.5 x 11 page.

A fluffy lion and a little curly-wool lamb curled up asleep together on the deck of the ark, a coil of rope and a bundle of hay beside them.

Jacob's spotted and speckled goats standing together in a stick fence pen, one little goat climbing on a rock and another chewing a leaf.

Balaam's patient donkey sitting down in the middle of a narrow vineyard path and refusing to walk, a stone wall on each side and grapevines on top.
Young shepherd David carrying a soft little lamb across his shoulders, a wooden shepherd's crook in one hand and three sheep following behind.

A small boy holding up a woven basket with five round loaves of bread and two fish inside, a grassy hillside behind him.
A smiling shepherd hugging the little lost sheep he has just found among the rocks, the rest of his flock waiting on the hill.
A mother hen spreading her wings wide while her fluffy chicks run in underneath, a few pebbles and grass tufts around her feet.
A little donkey walking down a road covered with palm branches and cloaks, children waving more palm branches on each side.
Fish cooking over a small campfire on a pebbly beach at sunrise, a loaf of bread beside the fire and a fishing boat pulled up on the sand.

prompts.name: Old Testament stories in order

fields.description: 24 Old Testament stories in Bible order, one scene per page: God creating light, the animals of creation, Noah building the ark, animals boarding two by two, the rainbow promise, the Tower of Babel, Abraham counting stars, Jacob's ladder, Joseph's coat, baby Moses in the reeds, the burning bush, crossing the Red Sea, Jericho's walls falling, Ruth in the barley field, young Samuel, David facing Goliath, fire on Mount Carmel, Jonah, the fiery furnace, Daniel and the lions, Queen Esther and Nehemiah rebuilding the walls.
fields.title: Old Testament Stories to Color

prompts.why: Sunday school teachers and Christian homeschoolers want the Old Testament in order, one story a week, and a 24-page book covers half the school year.
prompts.pageStyle: Black-and-white coloring page for a child aged 6 to 9: a clear Bible story scene with friendly, simply drawn people in robes and sandals, clear bold outlines, medium detail with a simple background that shows where the story happens, no shading, no grey, no words or letters, plain white background, portrait 8.5 x 11 page.
pages: The first day of creation: bright beams of light bursting through swirling dark clouds over an empty, rolling sea.
A brand-new green garden full of animals just made: a lion, an elephant, a rabbit, a deer and birds in the trees, with fruit trees and a winding river.
Noah on a ladder hammering planks onto the side of the huge wooden ark, his sons carrying beams and a saw and a bucket of pegs on the ground.
Animals walking up the ark's wooden ramp two by two: zebras, giraffes, bears and kangaroos, with Noah at the door counting them in.
Noah's family and the animals stepping out of the ark onto a grassy mountainside under a big rainbow, Noah kneeling beside a small stone altar.
People stacking mud bricks on the Tower of Babel, a tall spiral tower with ramps, ladders, baskets of bricks and workers on every level.
Old Abraham standing outside his tent at night with his arm raised, counting the countless stars, camels and a cooking fire beside the tent.
Jacob asleep on the ground with a stone for a pillow while angels walk up and down a shining stairway reaching into the clouds.
Young Joseph proudly wearing his long striped coat in a field, his eleven brothers watching from among their sheep and a water jug at his feet.
Joseph standing in Pharaoh's palace explaining the dreams, Pharaoh on his tall throne and a wall painting of seven fat cows and seven thin cows behind.
Baby Moses in a woven basket floating among tall reeds on the river, his big sister Miriam peeking out from behind the reeds to watch.
Moses barefoot on the rocky mountainside with his sandals beside him, kneeling before a bush full of flames that is not burning up, sheep nearby.
The Israelites walking across the dry seabed between two tall walls of water full of fish, Moses holding up his staff at the front.
Moses coming down the mountain carrying two large stone tablets with rounded tops, lightning clouds around the peak behind him.
Priests blowing long ram's horn trumpets as the walls of Jericho crumble, stones tumbling down and the people shouting behind them.
Ruth gathering barley stalks into a bundle in a golden field, Naomi waiting at the edge of the field with a basket and reapers working nearby.
Young Samuel sitting up in his bed in the temple at night, hearing his name called, a small oil lamp still glowing beside him.
Young shepherd David standing on a rock with his sling ready and five smooth stones in his bag, facing the giant Goliath in armour across the valley.
Fire falling from the sky onto Elijah's stone altar on Mount Carmel, water filling the trench around it and the crowd shielding their eyes.
The huge fish leaving Jonah on a sandy beach, Jonah sitting up surprised and dripping with seaweed, the walls of a big city far away.
Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego walking calmly inside a blazing furnace with a fourth shining figure beside them, the king staring in amazement.
Daniel standing calmly in the lions' den with an angel beside him, the lions lying down with their mouths shut and a stone over the opening above.
Queen Esther in a long robe and crown walking toward the king's throne, the king holding out his golden sceptre to welcome her.
Nehemiah directing workers rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem, people carrying stones, mixing mortar and fitting a big wooden gate.

prompts.name: The life of Jesus

fields.description: 24 scenes from the life of Jesus in Gospel order, one per page: the angel Gabriel visiting Mary, the journey to Bethlehem, the manger, shepherds and angels, the wise men, the boy Jesus in the temple, his baptism, calling the fishermen, water into wine, the woman at the well, the Sermon on the Mount, calming the storm, feeding the five thousand, walking on water, blessing the children, Zacchaeus, Palm Sunday, the Last Supper, Gethsemane, three empty crosses at sunset, the empty tomb and Pentecost.
fields.title: The Life of Jesus to Color

prompts.why: Sunday school teachers and Christian parents want the whole Gospel story in one book, from the angel's visit to Pentecost, ready for Christmas and Easter lessons.
prompts.pageStyle: Black-and-white coloring page for a child aged 6 to 9: a clear Gospel scene with gentle, simply drawn people in robes and sandals, clear bold outlines, medium detail with a simple background of hills, boats or village houses, no shading, no grey, no words or letters, plain white background, portrait 8.5 x 11 page.
pages: The angel Gabriel with wide wings appearing to young Mary in her small stone house, Mary surprised beside a water jar and a little oil lamp.
Joseph leading a donkey along a dusty road to Bethlehem with Mary riding on it, a bundle of belongings and the little town on a hill ahead.
Baby Jesus asleep in a wooden manger filled with hay in the stable, Mary and Joseph kneeling beside him, an ox and a donkey looking on.
Shepherds on a hillside at night looking up in wonder at a sky full of angels, their sheep gathered around a small campfire.
Three wise men on camels riding across the desert at night, following one big bright star, each holding a decorated gift box.
The boy Jesus aged twelve sitting among the teachers in the temple, scrolls open on a low table and the teachers listening closely.
John the Baptist in a camel-hair coat baptizing Jesus in the Jordan River, a dove flying down from opening clouds above them.
Jesus standing on the shore of the Sea of Galilee calling to Peter and Andrew, who are pulling a fishing net out of their boat.
Servants pouring water into six large stone jars at a wedding feast in Cana, Jesus beside them and guests dancing in the courtyard.
Jesus sitting beside a stone well talking with a Samaritan woman holding a clay water jar, a small village and hills behind them.
Jesus teaching a big crowd sitting on a grassy hillside by the lake, families with children, baskets and wildflowers all around.
Four friends lowering a man on a mat through a hole in a flat roof, Jesus and a crowded room looking up from below.
Jesus standing in a small fishing boat holding up his hand to calm a wild storm, the frightened disciples clinging to the mast and the oars.
A boy offering his basket of five loaves and two fish to Jesus, with a huge crowd sitting on the grass waiting to be fed.
Jesus walking on the waves at night toward the disciples' boat, Peter stepping out of the boat onto the water with one foot.
Jesus sitting on a rock with small children climbing onto his lap and gathering around him, their parents smiling nearby.
Short Zacchaeus perched on a branch of a sycamore tree peering over the crowd, Jesus standing below and looking up at him.
Jesus riding a donkey into Jerusalem while a crowd waves palm branches and lays cloaks on the road, the city gate ahead.
Jesus kneeling with a towel and a basin of water, washing Peter's feet, the other disciples watching from around the room.
The Last Supper: Jesus and his twelve disciples gathered around a long low table, Jesus breaking a round loaf of bread beside a cup.
Jesus kneeling in prayer beside a large rock among twisted olive trees in the garden of Gethsemane at night, a crescent moon above.
Three empty wooden crosses standing on a quiet hill at sunset, the city of Jerusalem in the distance and rays of light from the setting sun.
The empty tomb at sunrise with its round stone rolled away, an angel sitting on the stone and women arriving with jars of spices.
Pentecost: the disciples gathered in an upper room with small flames above their heads, a rushing wind blowing the curtains through the window.

prompts.name: Twenty-four parables Jesus told

fields.description: 24 parables Jesus told, one scene per page: the sower, the mustard seed, the yeast, the hidden treasure, the pearl, the fishing net, the wheat and the weeds, the lost sheep, the lost coin, the prodigal son, the good Samaritan, the rich fool's barns, the wise and foolish builders, the ten bridesmaids, the talents, the unforgiving servant, the vineyard workers, the two sons, the great banquet, the persistent widow, the Pharisee and the tax collector, the friend at midnight, the fig tree and new wine in old wineskins.
fields.title: The Parables of Jesus

prompts.why: Youth group leaders and Christian homeschoolers want a parables book for Bible study with older kids, one story to read and discuss on each page.
prompts.pageStyle: Black-and-white coloring page for ages 9 to 13: a detailed scene from a parable set in first-century Galilee and Judea, realistic people in robes and headcloths, fine clean outlines, detailed houses, fields, plants and landscape with many separate areas to color, no shading, no grey, no words or letters, plain white background, portrait 8.5 x 11 page.
pages: The sower: a farmer scattering seed from a shoulder bag across his field, birds pecking seeds on the path, rocks and thorn bushes at the edge and tall wheat growing in good soil.
The mustard seed: a huge mustard tree grown from a tiny seed, birds building nests in its spreading branches above a farmer resting in its shade.
The yeast in the dough: a woman kneading a big batch of dough in a wooden trough in her courtyard kitchen, a clay oven and bowls of flour beside her.
The hidden treasure: a farmer kneeling in a field, lifting the lid of a clay chest of coins he has just dug up, his shovel and ox plough nearby.
The pearl of great price: a merchant at a busy market stall holding up one large, perfect pearl in amazement, trays of jewels and baskets of shells around him.
The fishing net: fishermen on the shore sorting a full dragnet, putting good fish into baskets and throwing others back, their boat pulled onto the sand.
The wheat and the weeds: farmhands at harvest time pulling tall weeds from among the wheat and tying them in bundles, a barn and sheaves of wheat behind.
The lost sheep: a shepherd climbing down a rocky ravine to rescue one lamb caught in a thorn bush, the other ninety-nine sheep grazing on the hill above.
The lost coin: a woman sweeping the floor of her stone house by the light of an oil lamp, a small coin glinting in a corner under a stool.
The prodigal son: a father running down the road with open arms to hug his returning son in ragged clothes, the family house and fields behind them.
The good Samaritan: a traveler kneeling to bandage an injured man beside a rocky desert road, his donkey waiting and a priest walking away in the distance.
The rich fool: a wealthy farmer standing proudly in front of huge new barns overflowing with grain sacks, workers still building another barn beside them.
The wise and foolish builders: one house standing firm on a rock in a storm while a second house on the sand collapses into a rushing flood.
The ten bridesmaids: five young women holding brightly lit oil lamps at a wedding door at night, while five others run off looking for oil.
The talents: a servant proudly showing his master bags of coins he has earned, while another servant digs up a single buried coin under a tree.
The unforgiving servant: a servant on his knees before a king in a grand hall, begging for mercy, a royal accountant holding a long scroll of debts.
The workers in the vineyard: a landowner paying a line of workers one coin each at sunset, baskets of grapes and rows of vines behind them.
The two sons: a father in a vineyard speaking to two sons, one turning away with crossed arms and the other already carrying a grape basket to work.
The great banquet: servants leading poor, blind and lame guests from the streets into a long feast hall with tables full of bread, fruit and roast dishes.
The persistent widow: a widow knocking on the door of a judge's house again and again, the judge leaning out of the window with a frown.
The Pharisee and the tax collector: a proud man praying with his arms raised in the temple court, a humble tax collector at the back with his head bowed.
The friend at midnight: a man knocking on his neighbor's door under the stars, the neighbor opening the shutter with a sleepy face and three loaves in hand.
The fig tree with no fruit: a vineyard owner pointing at a bare fig tree while his gardener digs around its roots and spreads manure from a basket.
New wine in old wineskins: a wine seller pouring new wine into a fresh leather wineskin, an old cracked wineskin bursting and spilling beside him.

prompts.name: Scripture-inspired scenes for adults

fields.description: 24 detailed scenes drawn from scripture, one per page. Psalms: green pastures and still waters, a tree by streams, a sky full of stars, a deer at a brook, sparrows at the altar, sheltering wings, the sea creatures of Psalm 104, the hills of Psalm 121, instruments of praise. Prophets: eagles' wings, the wolf and the lamb, the desert in bloom, the potter's wheel, Ezekiel's river. Stories: Miriam's tambourine, Deborah's palm tree, Bethlehem's barley fields, the shepherds' fields, Galilee boats. Then lilies of the field, the vine, a cross at dawn, the empty tomb and the tree of life.
fields.title: Scenes of Faith

prompts.why: Christian adult colorists and church gift buyers want a devotional book with intricate scenes tied to verses they know, popular at Easter and Christmas.
prompts.pageStyle: Black-and-white adult coloring page: an intricate devotional scene with fine, crisp line work, detailed nature and decorative patterned areas in leaves, feathers, waves and filigree, many small areas to color, a balanced composition that fills the page, no shading, no grey, no words or verse text, plain white background, portrait 8.5 x 11 page.
pages: Psalm 23: a shepherd leading a flock through green pastures to still waters, a winding stream, willow trees and wildflowers filling the foreground.
Psalm 1: a tall leafy tree planted by streams of water, heavy with fruit, its roots spreading into the riverbank and ferns growing along the water.
Psalm 8: a hillside under a vast night sky crowded with stars, swirling galaxies and a crescent moon, a small figure gazing up beside a tent.
Psalm 42: a graceful deer drinking from a clear mountain brook that tumbles over rocks, pine trees and mossy stones all around.
Psalm 84: sparrows and swallows nesting in the carved stone niches of an ancient altar, a vine of leaves curling around the pillars.
Psalm 91: a great eagle spreading its sheltering wings over a nest of chicks, every feather drawn in fine layered detail against a rocky cliff.
Psalm 104: a teeming sea with whales, dolphins, octopus, fish shoals and sea turtles among waving seaweed and coral, a ship on the waves above.
Psalm 121: rolling hills and mountains at dawn, a winding path leading up toward them and a traveler with a staff looking toward the peaks.
Psalm 150: harps, lyres, trumpets, tambourines and cymbals arranged in a decorative circle with ribbons, olive branches and flowers.
Isaiah 40: a majestic eagle soaring on wide-spread wings over mountain peaks and clouds, rays of sunlight fanning out behind it.
Isaiah 11: a wolf lying beside a lamb and a leopard beside a young goat in a peaceful meadow, a lion and a calf resting under a tree.
Isaiah 35: a desert bursting into bloom, crocuses, lilies and wildflowers springing up among sand dunes and rocks, a stream running through.
Jeremiah 18: a potter's hands shaping a clay jar on a spinning wheel in a workshop, finished pots and jars lining wooden shelves around him.
Ezekiel 47: a river flowing from the temple doorway, lined on both banks with fruit trees, fish leaping in the water and fishermen casting nets.
Exodus 15: Miriam dancing with a tambourine on the seashore, women joining her with tambourines and the calm sea stretching behind them.
Judges 4: Deborah sitting under her tall palm tree in the hill country, people waiting to bring their questions, a clay jar and scrolls beside her.
Ruth 2: the barley fields of Bethlehem at harvest, reapers with sickles, sheaves stacked in rows and the little stone town on the hill behind.
Luke 2: shepherds' fields outside Bethlehem at night, sheep resting among stone walls, a lantern glowing and a sky full of stars and angels.
Mark 1: wooden fishing boats pulled up on the pebbly shore of the Sea of Galilee, nets drying on poles, baskets of fish and hills beyond the lake.
Matthew 6: lilies of the field growing in a lush meadow, birds of the air flying above them and a few wildflowers and grasses in fine detail.
John 15: a grapevine with heavy clusters of grapes and curling tendrils winding across a trellis, branches spreading out to fill the whole page.
A simple wooden cross standing on a hill at dawn, rays of light spreading behind it and a border of olive branches and wildflowers below.
The empty garden tomb at sunrise, its round stone rolled aside, lilies blooming at the entrance and the sun rising over olive trees.
Revelation 22: the tree of life growing on both banks of a crystal river through a heavenly city, its branches heavy with fruit and leaves.
